Spring Riding by Region

Spring arrives in Britain at different times depending on where you are. Cornwall is blooming while Scotland is still frozen. Understanding this gradient helps you choose the right destination for each spring month.

March: Head South

  • Cornwall/Devon (★★★★★): Mildest temperatures, daffodils blooming, coastal rides possible. The best March riding in Britain.
  • South Wales (★★★★): Gower Peninsula and Pembrokeshire are mild. The Wye Valley is sheltered and green.
  • Dorset/Hampshire (★★★★): New Forest and Jurassic Coast offer gentle spring riding.
  • Scottish Highlands (★★): Still cold, possibly snowy. Mountain passes may be closed. Not recommended for March.

April: Central England Opens Up

  • Cotswolds (★★★★★): Spring blossom, warm days, and the villages at their most photogenic.
  • Peak District (★★★★): The passes are clear, the moorland is greening. Good riding with quieter roads.
  • North Wales (★★★★): Snowdonia passes are rideable. The oak woodlands fill with birdsong.
  • Lake District (★★★): Improving but still cold at altitude. Valley rides are pleasant; passes may be chilly.

May: Everywhere Is Go

  • Scottish Highlands (★★★★★): The best month for Highland riding. Long days, no midges, empty roads.
  • Lake District (★★★★★): Before school holidays. The fells are green and the lakes are calm.
  • Yorkshire Dales (★★★★★): Wildflower meadows beginning. Perfect riding temperatures.
  • All regions (★★★★+): May is good everywhere. Choose your favourite landscape and go.
Spring's progression from south to north across Britain means you can extend the season by following the warmth. Start in Cornwall in March, ride the Cotswolds in April, and head to Scotland in May. You'll get three months of peak spring riding.

Spring Touring Tips

Spring riding requires flexibility. Check weather forecasts the morning of each ride and be prepared to adjust plans. A cold, wet March day in the Peak District can be rescued by dropping south to the Cotswolds where conditions are milder. Carry waterproofs even on sunny days — spring showers materialise quickly and without much warning.

Road surfaces in spring can be unpredictable. Winter frost damage creates potholes that haven't yet been repaired. Gravel and grit from winter treatments lingers in corners and on lesser-used roads. Ride smoothly and keep a watchful eye on the road surface, especially on B-roads and rural lanes.

Book accommodation flexibly if possible. Cancellation-friendly bookings allow you to move your tour dates by a few days to catch a good weather window, rather than being committed to specific dates regardless of conditions. This flexibility makes spring touring far more enjoyable. Read our What to Ride in Autumn: UK Regions Ranked for September-November guide for more. Read our What to Ride in Winter: UK Regions for December-February Touring guide for more. Read our UK Motorcycle Riding in March: Spring Begins guide for more.
keyTakeaways: Spring arrives south to north, so follow the warmth: Cornwall in March, the Cotswolds in April, Scotland in May.
March riding is best in Cornwall and Devon; the Scottish Highlands are still cold and passes may be closed.
April opens up central England, with the Cotswolds, Peak District, and North Wales all rideable.
May is good everywhere, with the Highlands offering long days, no midges, and empty roads.
Winter frost damage leaves fresh potholes and lingering grit in corners, so ride smoothly and watch the surface.

faq.q: Where should I ride in March?
faq.a: Head south. Cornwall and Devon offer the mildest temperatures, blooming daffodils, and possible coastal rides, making them the best March riding in Britain. South Wales, including the Gower and sheltered Wye Valley, is also good. Avoid the Scottish Highlands, which remain cold and possibly snowy with passes closed.

faq.q: When is Scotland ready for spring touring?
faq.a: May. It is arguably the best month for Highland riding, with long days, no midges yet, empty roads, and stunning light. In March and April the Highlands are still cold and unpredictable, so save them for late spring and ride southern and central England earlier in the season.

faq.q: What road hazards are specific to spring?
faq.a: Winter frost damage creates potholes that have not yet been repaired, and grit and gravel from winter treatments linger in corners and on lesser-used roads. Ride smoothly, keep a watchful eye on the surface, especially on B-roads, and be aware that early-season tyres and skills both need easing back in.

faq.q: How should I plan spring rides around weather?
faq.a: Stay flexible. Check the forecast the morning of each ride and be ready to adjust. A cold, wet day in the Peak District can be rescued by dropping south to the milder Cotswolds. Carry waterproofs even on sunny days, and use cancellation-friendly bookings so you can shift dates to catch a good weather window.
